desc:
Drupal migration and version upgrade moves your content into Drupal from WordPress or another platform, or brings an older Drupal site to the current version. Ecom Swift LLC maps, tests and runs the move, with redirects for old addresses.

## What is a Drupal migration?

A Drupal migration is the planned transfer of your pages, posts, images, users and categories from an existing site into a new or upgraded Drupal site. The source can be WordPress, another content management system, static files or an older Drupal installation. A version upgrade is a related job: moving an older Drupal site to the current supported release, where content and settings are carried across a large structural change.

Moving by hand means copying and pasting hundreds of pages and fixing broken images afterwards. A scripted migration does the same job consistently and can be repeated until it is right.

## Why migrations go wrong

Most migration problems come from skipped planning. Content types do not match, authors are lost, image links point to the old server and page addresses change without redirects. The visible result is broken pages, missing images and visitors who land on a not found error from a link that used to work.

Search engines react to the same problems. When old addresses stop working and no redirect points to the new page, the pages that earned visibility can fall out of results. Careful mapping and redirects reduce that risk, though we cannot promise how search engines will respond.

## How a careful migration protects your results

A careful migration protects what the old site built. Your articles, your links from other sites and your visitors' bookmarks all continue to work. Editors start on the new site with a clean, consistent structure instead of a pile of imported leftovers.

Doing a trial run first also protects your launch. You see real samples, such as a post with images, an author page and a category list, and correct the mapping before the full move. The final run then holds no surprises.

## What a good Drupal migration includes

- An inventory of what exists: content types, counts, authors, categories, media and menus.
- A mapping from each source type to a Drupal content type and field.
- A sample migration for your approval before the full run.
- Images and attached files carried across and linked correctly.
- Authors and user accounts moved where needed, with roles reviewed.
- Categories and tags recreated as Drupal taxonomy terms.
- Redirects from old addresses to new ones, in a reviewed list.
- A side by side check of source and result for important pages.
- For upgrades, the path from an older Drupal version to the current one.
- Cutover support on launch day.

## What we do

We begin with the inventory and agree the mapping with you. We build the migration on a staging site and run a small sample, which you review. After corrections we run the complete move and compare pages against the source.

We then build the redirect list from the old addresses to the new ones and test it. The Basic package covers a first move of a smaller site with a sample to approve. Standard adds a larger volume, users, taxonomy and redirects. Premium covers a complete migration or upgrade, menus, blocks, the media library and help on launch day. We use your old site as the source and leave it untouched until you are happy.

## What to do and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Clean out outdated pages before the move, not after.
- Keep the old site online until the new one is approved.
- Give us a list of your most important pages to check first.
- Plan redirects early, since they matter most for search visibility.
- Freeze content edits in the last days before the final run.

**Avoid:**
- Moving every old draft, test page and unused image.
- Changing page addresses without a redirect plan.
- Editing the old site while the final migration runs.
- Skipping the sample, since errors are cheapest to fix there.
- Switching your domain before the new site has been checked.

## Who this is for

This suits an organization moving from WordPress that wants the control Drupal offers over content types and permissions. It suits a site still running an older Drupal release that needs to catch up with supported versions, and a company merging several small sites into one.

## What we need from you

Tell us where the content lives now, and give us access to export it or to read from the source site, as a collaborator or administrator user. We never ask for passwords. Send a list of the pages that matter most and any address changes you plan. We will confirm the mapping before we move anything.
